overview: A chassis kit is the structural starting point for almost every wheeled hobby robot: a pre-cut acrylic or plastic base plate with mounting holes already positioned for a couple of common gear motors, a caster wheel for balance, and usually a second deck plate for stacking a microcontroller, battery, and breadboard on top. Buying one instead of designing custom brackets from scratch removes an entire category of early mechanical-design problems, letting a first robotics project focus on the electronics and code rather than on getting motor mounting geometry right.
simpleSummary: A ready-made plastic base plate with motors and wheels attached, the starting frame for a wheeled robot.

specifications.material: Acrylic or ABS plastic, laser-cut or injection molded
specifications.driveConfiguration: 2WD (two driven wheels + caster) or 4WD (four driven wheels, no caster needed)
specifications.mountingPattern: Pre-drilled holes sized for standard TT gear motors and M3 screws

pinMap.name: Motor Mount (Left)
pinMap.function: Pre-drilled mounting position for the left drive motor, sized for standard TT gear motor tabs.
pinMap.gotcha: Motor mount hole spacing varies slightly between chassis brands — verify your specific gear motor fits before drilling anything new.

pinMap.name: Motor Mount (Right)
pinMap.function: Pre-drilled mounting position for the right drive motor.

pinMap.name: Caster Mount
pinMap.function: Mounting position for a caster wheel (2WD chassis only) providing a third point of balance.

pinMap.name: Deck Standoffs
pinMap.function: Threaded standoff posts for mounting a second deck plate above the main chassis, for stacking electronics.

pinMap.name: Component Mounting Holes
pinMap.function: General-purpose holes across the plate for zip-tying or screwing down a battery holder, driver board, or breadboard.

useCases.title: First wheeled robot build
useCases.scenario: The standard starting platform for line-following, obstacle-avoidance, or Bluetooth-controlled robot projects.

useCases.title: Sensor payload platform
useCases.scenario: Stack a second deck with additional sensors/electronics above the base motor/battery layer.

oftenConfusedWith: 3D-printed custom chassis (more design flexibility, more upfront effort)
oftenUpgradedTo: Custom-designed 3D-printed or laser-cut chassis once specific sensor/mounting needs outgrow a generic kit
